PRODUCTNAME splits the cost of a shared, self-hosted Grafana Mimir across its tenants. It reads Mimir's own metrics and tells you what share of each shared component each tenant is responsible for. This is the first release.

## What it does

`PRODUCTNAME cost` covers three cost pools, and splits each one by the thing that physically makes it grow:

| Pool | Split by |
|---|---|
| Ingester memory | active series, averaged over the window, divided by the replication factor |
| Query path (query-frontend + querier) | fetched chunk bytes, falling back to samples processed, series fetched, then query seconds |
| Ruler CPU | rule-evaluation seconds |

- **Resources first.** By default you get shares and an equivalent replica count ("`analytics` uses the equivalent of 5.0 of your 8 ingesters").
- **Currency only from your prices.** Add a price per replica to `PRODUCTNAME.yaml` and you get currency. There's no built-in pricing database and no fitted coefficient. An unpriced pool says "not costed", and a total across pools says which pools it covers.
- **Absence isn't zero.** Anything it couldn't measure says "not measured", never 0.
- **Every figure has a trail.** Each pool lists the query, the replication factor, the write path, the rule evaluation mode and the price behind it.
- **Read-only.** It's one binary. It sends `GET` requests to your Mimir and nothing else, and it needs no agent and no database.

The pools it doesn't model yet (ingester write path, object storage, store-gateway, compactor) are listed as not modelled in every report.

Drill-downs: `cost --rule-outputs` names the recording rules that write a tenant's series. `report` attributes ruler workload to rule groups, or to single rules if you give it Mimir's ruler query-stats log.

## Install

Linux and macOS (amd64, arm64) and Windows (amd64) binaries are attached below, with `checksums.txt`.

```sh
VERSION=0.1.0 OS=linux ARCH=amd64   # or OS=darwin, ARCH=arm64
BASE=https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/download/v${VERSION}
curl -sSLO "$BASE/PRODUCTNAME_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
curl -sSLO "$BASE/checksums.txt"
grep "PRODUCTNAME_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" checksums.txt | sha256sum -c
tar xzf "PRODUCTNAME_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" PRODUCTNAME

# Or with Go 1.27.1+
go install github.com/OWNER/REPO/cmd/PRODUCTNAME@v0.1.0
```

You need a Mimir whose own `cortex_*` metrics are scraped into one of its tenants. Point `--metrics-tenant` at that tenant (the one that holds Mimir's metrics, not one you want to cost):

```sh
PRODUCTNAME cost --config PRODUCTNAME.yaml --metrics-tenant meta --since 24h
```

[Getting started](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/docs/getting-started.md) walks through a first report. To run it in Kubernetes as a Job or a daily CronJob, see [`deploy/kubernetes/`](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/deploy/kubernetes/README.md).

## What was validated

PRODUCTNAME was checked against a staging Mimir where the right answer is known. All of the evidence is indexed in [`dev/staging/results/README.md`](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/dev/staging/results/README.md).

**Both write paths pass 87 of 87 checks** on this release's code:

- [Ingest storage](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/dev/staging/results/2026-10-22-ingest/report.md) (Kafka, 3 zones).
- [Classic](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/dev/staging/results/2026-10-22-classic/report.md) (RF=3, 3 zones). PRODUCTNAME read the replication factor of 3 from Mimir and divided it out: `steady` reads 30,022 active series against 30,022 delivered.

Each run used Mimir 3.2.0 (Helm chart `mimir-distributed` 6.2.0, microservices mode, remote rule evaluation), 8 synthetic tenants whose delivered series, samples, queries and rules are recorded by the load generator, and windows of 1h, 30m and 10m. The 1h window contains an ingester rolling restart. The 30m and 10m windows are clean, and they're checked at ±1%. In both runs:

- **Shares summed to 100%** in all three pools, in every window.
- **Active series matched ground truth.** Every tenant was inside its band in the clean windows, and the five constant-size tenants matched exactly. PRODUCTNAME's figure equalled Mimir's own gauge, read independently, for all 9 tenants (the 8 synthetic ones plus the metrics tenant).
- **Tenants that joined or left mid-window were averaged over the whole window** (see #66 below).
- **The query-heavy and rule-heavy tenants dominated their pools**, which the workload is built to produce: `dashboards` had 93.2–97.6% of the query path and `rules` had 87.1–90.7% of ruler CPU, across both runs and all windows.
- **`--rule-outputs` counts were exact** for all 8 tenants.
- **The write path and the rule evaluation mode were detected correctly.**

**Validation found a real bug, and it's fixed.** The [first ingest-storage run](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/dev/staging/results/2026-10-22-ingest-before-66-fix/report.md) passed 79 of 83. All four failures had one cause, [#66](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/66): `avg_over_time` averages only over the points where a series exists, and Mimir drops a tenant's active-series gauge once it has none. So a tenant that joined or left mid-window was averaged over its own presence and overstated. The fix averages over the whole window and counts absence as zero. The two 87/87 runs above are on the fix.

**Local rule evaluation** was checked in [a separate run](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/dev/staging/results/2026-10-22-ingest-local-eval/report.md). It detected `local` mode, and tenants that never query read "not measured" in the query path, never 0. It passed 33 of 34. The one failure (`churn`) is a Mimir effect, not PRODUCTNAME's: switching the ruler mode rolled every ingester, and a restarted ingester only re-counts series that receive new samples. Mimir's own gauge read the same as PRODUCTNAME. The report explains it at the top.

**What this doesn't show.** Staging is one cloud container (k3s in Docker, 4 vCPU), not a multi-node cluster. Every costed tenant is synthetic. Windows are 1h at most, with no day-long soak. Pools 6 and 7 are checked by ranking, not absolute value. And it doesn't check whether active series is the right driver of ingester memory, only that PRODUCTNAME reads it correctly. Each report lists its own limits.

## Known issues

- **`--rule-outputs` shows up in the query path** ([#61](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/61)). Its count queries run as each tenant, so a later window that includes the run charges them to that tenant's query path. A tenant that never queries can go from "not measured" to "0 B". The report says so when it happens.
- **Windows binaries are built but untested.**
- **Only Mimir 3.2.0 is tested**, and only on a single-container staging environment with synthetic tenants (see above). The driver metrics are long-standing `cortex_*` metrics, but we haven't checked their names and labels on other versions.
- **Ingester rollouts make pool 1 read low.** While an ingester replica is down, the averaged active-series figure reads low. We measured 9% on the dev rig. On staging, the windows that overlap a rollout are checked with a ±15% band.
- **Remote rule evaluation mixes ruler queries into the query path.** Under remote evaluation, the ruler's queries go through the query-frontend, so they're counted in the query path. The report says which mode it detected. You can state the mode with `inventory.ruler_evaluation`.
- **No client certificates or custom CA.** It supports bearer tokens and HTTP basic auth, and trusts the system CA store.
- **One window at a time.** It doesn't compare windows or store history yet.

## What's next

In the order set out in [ADR 0004](https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/v0.1.0/docs/adr/0004-finops-pivot-scope-and-sequencing.md):

1. Comparing windows ("up 4pp on last week, and why")
2. Daily rollups to a store you own
3. A change timeline built from ruler API snapshots
4. The remaining pools: write path, object storage, store-gateway and compactor

Reports from other Mimir versions and topologies are the most useful thing you can send. Please include the `--format json` output, or the assumption table for the figure that looks wrong.
